blocks.text: Zscaler Device Investigation provides administrators with a comprehensive view of all endpoint details, including real-time device health status. For any unhealthy devices, errors are clearly highlighted with detailed descriptions to ease troubleshooting. This feature also offers visibility into Shadow IT by listing all detected applications on the endpoint, with threat intelligence to flag malicious and suspicious software and the sensitive data stored on the endpoint. This streamlined solution empowers organizations to maintain robust endpoint security and compliance.
The Device Investigation page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Identify and display sensitive files stored locally, ensuring administrators can address potential data security risks effectively.
Use the detailed error descriptions to troubleshoot the causes of unhealthy devices.
View device details such as Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) version, Zscaler Client Connector version, Endpoint Data Scan status, anti-tampering status, and so on for individual endpoints.

blocks.text: On the Device Investigation page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Device Investigation), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter the data for a specific OS, Endpoint Name, Endpoint Health, Error Type, or Last Connected. You can add filters by clicking the plus icon. The available options are as follows: Endpoint DLP Version, Endpoint DLP Policy Version, Device Control Policy Version, Endpoint DLP Mode, Zscaler Client Connector Version, and Anti Tampering Status.
Export: Click Export to download the Device Investigation details in a CSV format.
View a list of endpoints. For each endpoint, you can view:
Endpoint ID: The unique ID of the endpoint.

Endpoint Name: The name of the endpoints connected to the user's device. Click the endpoint name to open a drawer that shows all the endpoint's details. To learn more, see Analyzing Device Investigation Details.
See image.
User Name: The email address of the user. Click a user to open a drawer that shows scan details for that user. To learn more, see Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan Details for a User.
Endpoint Health: Indicates the health of the endpoint. If the endpoint is unhealthy, you can hover over the error to view the reason.
Endpoint DLP Version: Indicates the DLP version of the endpoint.
Zscaler Client Connector Version: Indicates the current version of Zscaler Client Connector.
Endpoint DLP Status: Indicates the Endpoint DLP status.
Nearby Sharing Status: Indicates whether the device control rule for nearby sharing is set to allow, block, or whether the rule is disabled for the endpoint.
Allowed: Endpoint DLP enables nearby sharing but does not override or enforce it if another product blocks the nearby sharing.
Blocked: Endpoint DLP prevents file transfers to nearby sharing devices.
Disabled: Endpoint DLP does not restrict nearby sharing.
Endpoint Data Scan Status: Indicates if the Endpoint Data Scan reporting is enabled or disabled for the endpoint.
Anti-Tampering Status: Indicates if anti-tampering is enabled or disabled for an endpoint. To learn more about anti-tampering, see Anti-Tampering for Zscaler Client Connector.
Last Connected: The date and time when the last time the endpoint was connected.
Modify the table and its columns.

blocks.text: Use the arrows at the bottom of the page to go to view the next entries. You can also select the number of entries you want to view in the table (3, 5, or 15 rows).
